newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm oil stable in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm oil stable in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally stable in quiet late trading on Friday as traders remained cautious while waiting for the Malaysian monthly output figure due at the end of this week.

They said palm olein was stable at 1,415-20 rupiah in Jakarta, down from 1,420-25 rupiah at Thursday's close. Some offers were also heard at 1,425-30 rupiah/kg. Crude palm oil was on offer at around 1,250 rupiah/kg in the North Sumatran city of Medan, where it was last done at 1,252 at a tender.
"The market is a little bit cautious as it waits for the Malaysian output figure on Saturday," said one trader.
"Traders expect the figure to give some direction to the market next week," he said.
Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) is expected to release its February crop data covering output, exports and stocks on Saturday.
Traders said local buying interest stayed thin on the back of a steady decline in palm olein prices, adding that values could continue to soften next week.
The Malaysian crop forecaster, Ivan Wong, released his crop report on Malaysia on Friday, but Indonesian traders said their eyes were on the PORLA report.
Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Oriental Miracle will leave on Friday for Tanjung Priok, Jakarta, with 1,200 tonnes of palm olein. - Jakarta newsroom + 6221 384-6364
